newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Amplats, unions sign peace accord.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Amplats, unions sign peace accord.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) and labour unions said on Tuesday they had signed a peace accord aimed at ending sporadic outbreaks of violence at the group's mines.

Amplats said a Monday peace summit had been attended by unions and management and all parties had agreed to commit themselves to resolving the labour unrest situation which has claimed at least two lives in the past month.
"The peace summit must be seen as a first step in resolving the situation which has arisen and will be followed by the appropriate actions to address the issue.
"The full commitment expressed by all parties attending the summit bodes well for the speedy resolution of the problem," said a joint statement after the signing of a declaration of intent.
Amplats' Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd, the world's largest platinum mine, has been plagued by a long-running dispute over union representation.
It was hit late in May by a two-day wildcat strike affecting 15 percent of production.
The powerful National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said late last month that it was considering unspecified action after the murder of two NUM members at Rustenburg.
But Amplats and the unions said following the summit, all parties committed themselves to eliminate all acts of violence and ensure the maintenance of peace.
Rusplats produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 1996.
